policies.description: Before calling remove_group_membership, verify that all required parameters (group_id and user_id) are provided and not missing, as the operation requires mandatory fields to be validated.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Execute remove_group_membership as a single validated operation; do not combine it with other actions in the same request, and ensure the required data is present before proceeding.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description: Confirm that the user identified by user_id is active (users.active = true) before removing their group membership, as updates involving users must only affect active accounts.
references: User Status: Ensure any user being assigned to (assigned_to) or updated is users.active = true.

policies.description: When a request is received to remove a user from a group, first retrieve the requester's user record using a lookup tool (e.g., `get_user` with the requester's `user_id` obtained from the authentication token). If the retrieved `role` is **admin** or **manager**, proceed to call `remove_group_membership`. For any other role, immediately respond with a `403 Forbidden` error and do not invoke `remove_group_membership`.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.description: Validate that the specified group_id exists in the system via a verified lookup before attempting to remove the membership.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, rely solely on verified API results.
Referential Integrity: Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied.

policies.description: Before invoking `remove_group_membership`, verify: (1) the group exists (using `list_user_groups` or `find_group_by_name`); (2) the user exists and has `active=true` (using `get_user` or `list_users` with an `active` filter); (3) a membership record linking the group and user is present (using `list_group_members`). If a `member_id` is supplied, confirm it matches the retrieved membership record. If any of these checks fail, halt the operation and return a policy‑violation message.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, rely solely on verified API results.
Referential Integrity: Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied.

policies.description: If a member_id is supplied, ensure it corresponds exactly to the provided group_id and user_id, maintaining referential integrity of the group‑membership record.
references: Referential Integrity: Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied.

policies.policy_name: Administrator Role Required for Group Membership Removal
policies.description: Only a user with the Administrator role may invoke `remove_group_membership`, because Administrators have full CRUD access across all tables, which includes user‑group management. If the calling user does not hold the `admin` role, the operation must be halted and a 403 Forbidden response returned.
references: | **Administrator** (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. |

archive.policy_name: No Approval Bypass for Group Membership Changes
archive.description: When removing a user from a group, the assistant must not bypass any required approvals. Changes that affect system‑administration settings such as group memberships must follow the normal approval workflow; attempting to delete a membership without the appropriate approval must cause the operation to halt with a policy violation.
references: Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings.
